key_insight: Three-dimensional DSMC captures measured jet–crossflow interference pressures, while two-dimensional simulations reproduce qualitative patterns but overpredict peak pressure about twelvefold.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of reaction-control-jet interference in rarefied hypersonic flight requires three-dimensional kinetic modeling rather than a planar approximation.
method: Revisit a 1975 DLR helium-jet experiment in Mach 11–12 air crossflow.
Compare 2D and 3D DSMC at three freestream densities spanning Knudsen numbers 0.021–0.125.
Evaluate wall pressures, boundary layers, shock topology, and planar resolution convergence.
evidence_signal: Across all three densities, 3D DSMC matches measured interference-pressure lobe peaks within 25% and peak positions within 3 mm.
watch_item: Both 2D and 3D simulations overpredict plate-alone wall pressure by 50–75%, and validation of jet strength and forces remains ongoing.
paper_title: Kinetic study of Reaction-Control-Jet Interference in Rarefied Hypersonic Crossflow
